Restart Budget of the Break-Point Terms

Source: R/boot_restart.R
seg_boot_total.Rd

Returns the largest n_boot set in a break-point term that is written directly in an equation of the specification, and zero when there is no such term. A break-point term nested inside a parameter of modelterms7::nl() is not counted. statmod_boot_restart() takes this number as the maximum number of proposals that it tries.

Usage

seg_boot_total(spec)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec(). The terms of every equation are examined.

Value

A single non-negative integer. It is zero when no term sets n_boot, and statmod() does not run the restart loop for a budget of zero.

Details

The number is set in the term. modelterms7::seg(), modelterms7::jump() and modelterms7::jseg() each take n_boot, with a default of 10, because the objective of these terms has spurious local optima that the restarts search for. The restarts are run by this package, which can refit the model.

A model with two break-point terms that set n_boot to 10 and to 25 gets 25. The restart loop works on all of the terms together, since a proposal is a configuration of positions for every break-point term in the model, so the budget is a single number and the largest of the set values is used.

See also

statmod_boot_restart(), which spends this budget, modelterms7::seg() for where the number is set.
